On 19 October 2026, Judge Simon Birt at the High Court dismissed two claims against Uber totaling about £340 million. About 13,000 black cab drivers sought nearly £200 million and a Kabbee and Iride claimant about £140 million. Filed in 2024, the suits alleged Uber misled Transport for London to obtain its 2012 private-hire licence and diverted business from traditional operators. Uber denied the allegations. An Uber spokesperson said the court dismissed all of the claims entirely at the earliest opportunity and put these legacy matters firmly in the past. RGL Management, running the claimants' case, said it was very disappointed and is considering all options available to the claimant cab drivers with the legal team. Mishcon de Reya notified Uber by letter in 2019 then went silent four and a half years after a litigation funder withdrew. Outlets differ on the headline sum, with some citing £250 million ($333 million) and others about $453 million. Uber and Lyft Drivers in California Now Have a Gig Worker Rarity: A Union
Independent contractors, especially gig workers, aren’t generally afforded the rights and privileges of employees. Most don’t have access to healthcare, retirement plans — or unions. But that all changed recently for Uber and Lyft workers in California.
On Sept. 9, the California Public Employment Relations Board certified the California Gig Workers Union as the bargaining organization for drivers working for covered transportation network companies. For now, that means Uber and Lyft. Soon, drivers may be able to negotiate over pay and other working conditions.
Start Shopping: I'm an Auto Expert: These Used Cars Could Get Cheaper Throughout 2026
Earn Easily: 8 Low-Effort Ways To Make Passive Income (You Can Start This Week)
More Than 100,000 California Drivers Could Be Affected
The Transportation Network Company Drivers Labor Relations Act, which took effect Jan. 1, 2026, gives rideshare drivers the right to organize and bargain collectively while retaining their status as independent contractors.
For this all to happen, at least 30% of active drivers had to authorize the union to act as their bargaining representative. After reaching the 10% level in June, support topped the threshold required for certification by August. This led to formal certification by the PERB on Sept. 9.
The potential reach of the union is significant. As of the first half of 2026, PERB reported 100,307 active transportation network company drivers, with the vast majority working with Uber and Lyft. Those two companies alone accounted for more than 99% of the 75.2 million covered rides reported during that period.
A Union Doesn't Guarantee Drivers Higher Pay
A union might fight for workers’ rights, but it doesn’t mean the Uber and Lyft drivers will automatically get raises or new benefits. The ultimate financial effect on drivers, if any, will depend on the union’s course of action and what it can get companies to agree to.
If you’re considering taking a job as an Uber or Lyft driver because of the union news, be aware that the new union doesn’t guarantee higher pay or real benefits. Each bargaining proposal will be fought for by the union, but nothing goes into effect until an actual agreement is reached.
California Is Testing a Different Model for Gig Work
The bigger story may be the unusual combination California has created.
The state has traditionally separated independent contractors from traditional employees for legal purposes. But this new system allows drivers to remain independent contractors while still potentially benefitting from the collective bargaining rights of the union.
As this is all somewhat experimental, it’s worth watching to see how it all plays out in California and whether similar approaches succeed elsewhere in the country. A strong collective bargaining agreement for Uber and Lyft drivers could ultimately alter the economics of rideshare driving for people who rely on these gig jobs for either supplemental income or full-time earnings. Whether or not any agreements alter the pricing structure for riders is also a worthy consideration.
For the time being, nothing about a driver’s paycheck will change immediately simply because the union was certified. But with the earnings of more than 100,000 active California rideshare drivers potentially being affected, these new developments mark a significant change for one of America’s best-known gig-economy jobs.

Uber can use its existing restaurant and delivery infrastructure while ezCater brings its corporate catering business, according to Reuters.
The deal also strengthens Uber’s business-focused segment, which serves corporate customers. Gross bookings in this segment grew by more than 40% in the second quarter, according to Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt. Devitt said bringing workplace buyers into Uber’s ecosystem could also help strengthen its membership business.
Uber Eats has a larger global reach, but DoorDash remains the biggest player in the US food delivery market, according to analysts cited by Reuters. Buying ezCater could help Uber close some of that gap in the US. Corporate catering gives Uber another way to attract food-delivery customers beyond regular restaurant orders.

Uber said ezCater’s average order value is above $400. The company expects the acquisition to boost margins. Larger orders can make the delivery business more valuable because Uber can generate more business from each corporate transaction.
The ezCater deal comes only months after Uber agreed in July to buy German food-delivery company Delivery Hero for $14.8 billion. That deal is aimed at creating the largest food-delivery group outside China, according to Reuters. Together, the two deals show that Uber is putting significant money into expanding its delivery operations.
Uber’s delivery business accounted for about 37% of the company’s total revenue in the second quarter. It has also been Uber’s biggest growth driver in recent times. The ezCater acquisition therefore fits into Uber’s wider strategy of making delivery a bigger part of its business.
Uber’s shares have fallen about 15% this year as investors consider how the company will compete if robotaxis changes the ride-hailing industry. The possible rise of autonomous taxis could put pressure on Uber’s traditional ride-hailing business. Expanding food delivery and corporate services gives Uber another source of growth as the future of traditional ride-hailing becomes less certain.
The deal gives Uber access to a corporate catering platform that already handles billions of dollars in bookings. It adds high-value orders, brings more companies into Uber’s ecosystem and expands Uber’s business customer base. It also gives Uber another way to compete in the US food-delivery market while strengthening its fastest-growing business. The acquisition still needs regulatory approval. Uber expects the deal to close in the coming months, according to Reuters.

Uber Technologies (UBER) Is Generating Cash, but Can Robotaxi Spending Preserve Its Valuation?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:13 PM CDT 5 min read
Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) is approaching a difficult valuation test: its established ride-hailing network is producing more cash, while autonomous vehicles threaten to change who controls transportation demand. On September 2, the Financial Times reported plans to eliminate 3,300 corporate jobs, or about 10% of the global workforce, as the company redirects resources toward robotaxis. Analysts at Citi estimated roughly $825 million of annual savings. That would cover only a fraction of Uber's stated commitment of more than $10 billion to autonomous-vehicle expansion, so the investment case still turns on whether the new spending protects or dilutes future returns.
Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) reported more than $58 billion of second-quarter 2026 gross bookings, up 22% year-over-year, and revenue of $14.19 billion, up 12%. Trailing twelve-month free cash flow exceeded $10 billion for the first time. Those numbers show why investors cannot assess the robotaxi transition simply as an existential threat: Uber has an existing earnings engine capable of helping fund the change. But gross bookings are customer transaction value, not company revenue, and that distinction matters when forecasting how much incremental driverless demand Uber can monetize.
Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) sits on the second spot on our list of the 10 best undervalued stocks to buy now according to Reddit, ranked by second-quarter hedge fund holders. The ranking raises a useful comparison: why did an established mobility platform outrank eight other potential value opportunities when its most important competitive question remains unsettled?
Uber Technologies (UBER) Is Generating Cash, but Can Robotaxi Spending Preserve Its Valuation?
Uber Technologies, Inc.'s network could become more valuable if manufacturers and fleet owners use it to fill empty seats. Management said autonomous vehicles were operating through its platform in seven cities, with a goal of 15 by the end of 2026. In early deployments, Uber reported roughly 25 to 30 trips per vehicle per day, a utilization rate that is financially important because expensive fleets earn nothing while parked.
However, operators such as Alphabet's Waymo may eventually acquire riders directly. An autonomous fleet can also shift bargaining power away from millions of independent drivers toward a smaller set of well-capitalized suppliers. The regulatory emphasis on hybrid fleets, as described by the Financial Times on September 5, therefore has a commercial dimension. Our earlier examination of whether Uber's economic moat can survive the robotaxi transition explores the same question from the perspective of network effects and potential disintermediation.
A second expansion complicates the economics. Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) agreed to acquire Delivery Hero in a transaction valuing the business at approximately €13 billion, with closing expected in the second half of 2027. Management hopes to add $1.2 billion to Delivery Hero's operating profit through a combination of efficiency and cross-selling. Yet the acquired business is loss-making, and realizing revenue synergies across many markets is harder to verify than simply removing duplicated overhead.
The Seeking Alpha data shows Uber Technologies, Inc. (NYSE:UBER) at 15.12 times trailing GAAP earnings and 21.81 times forward GAAP earnings; the comparable non-GAAP multiples are 24.00 and 20.65, respectively. The difference between forward GAAP and non-GAAP readings is a reminder that the definition of earnings materially changes the apparent valuation. On non-GAAP forward earnings, the multiple is around 30% below Uber's five-year average of 29.60, but still above the sector median of 18.86.
The earnings trajectory also resists a simplistic cheap-stock label. Seeking Alpha shows forward GAAP EPS growth of approximately negative 0.22%, even as forward EBITDA growth is 28.74% and expected three-to-five-year EPS compound growth reaches 27.30%. Those figures can coexist when accounting items and the time horizons differ, but the gap demands attention. A discounted multiple against Uber's own history is not automatically a discount to its future obligations.
There is also a question of cash availability. Our examination of Uber's growing insurance bill and whether operating cash can keep up distinguishes insurance reserves from unrestricted cash. That matters when future robotaxi capital requirements compete with insurance collateral, acquisitions, and repurchases. Management has described an intention to devote about half of free cash flow to buybacks.
Institutional Money Is Watching the Transition
Insider Monkey's Q2 2026 13F database counted 151 bullish hedge funds, down from 153 in Q1, suggesting a broadly stable but not strengthening institutional base. At September 30, 48.75 million shares were sold short, up from 45.12 million on August 31, equivalent to 2.48% of the float. Neither measure proves a specific view about autonomous vehicles, but the increase in short positions sits alongside the company's substantial investment commitments.
Wells Fargo raised its target to $92 from $89 on October 5 and maintained Overweight, identifying durable U.S. mobility trips growth in 2027 as important while Waymo scales. That is the relevant test: if trips, margins, and free cash flow hold up during deployment, the valuation gap to Uber Technologies, Inc.'s historical multiple could narrow. If billions in fleet spending produce limited incremental economics or direct robotaxi competition reduces platform relevance, today's forward earnings estimates could require revision. A separate analysis of what the market is actually pricing into Uber's robotaxi risk lays out why strong cash flow and a declining share price can coexist.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of UBER as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. Stop Overpaying for Uber: How to Score Senior Discounts on Rideshare Apps
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:36 AM CDT 5 min read
A little more than a decade ago, getting into a stranger's car and telling them where to take you would be viewed as ill-advised at best. But with the rise of rideshare apps like Uber, Lyft and others, nothing seems more ordinary. The system comes with a lot of benefits; it tends to be cheaper than traditional taxis, it works effectively in most places and you can get practically wherever you want to go.
Combine the rideshare phenomenon with more traditional modes of transportation, and the world has gotten more mobile than ever before with plenty of options to travel. Alas, almost all those options still cost money. Luckily for seniors, there are also plenty of opportunities to save money while getting around.
Want more ways to save money? Sign up for The Penny Hoarder's free newsletter today.
How to Score Senior Discounts on Ridesharing Apps
The bigger rideshare companies all have their own apps, and if you know what to look for, there are loads of ways to save.
When using any of these apps, keep an eye out for promo codes that can help you save even more. In recent promotions, Lyft and Uber both advertise promo codes which give up to 50% discounts to new riders, regardless of your age.
Lyft doesn't offer a generalized senior discount for their basic service, but through their Lyft Silver program, seniors can use a simplified interface, find better vehicle matches (easier entry and exit) and get support to book their ride through Lyft.
Lyft's subscription service Lyft Pink does offer discounts with plans starting at $9.99 (or $99/year). For those who need to travel on a regular basis or have a busy schedule, Pink can help you save a bundle.
Additionally, many cities partner with Lyft to offer discounted rides to those 60 and older. In Charleston, South Carolina, CARTA offers seniors Lyft or Uber trips for as little as $5 each way within a fixed-route area.
Similar to Lyft, Uber doesn't offer a specific senior discount, but it does partner with municipalities to offer discounted rides for those 60 and older.
Also similar to Lyft, if you're a frequent rider, you can save money with a membership. An Uber One membership costs $9.99 (or $96/year) and lets you earn 5% back on rides and includes a $0 delivery fee for food and grocery orders.
GoGoGrandparent.com connects you to rideshare services and arranges deliveries of groceries and medications. Despite the name, anyone over 18 can order a ride and you can use it from any phone that generates tones by the press of a button — meaning, you don't need a smartphone. It features a simple menu and a live service that can help customers find the best and cheapest options. It also includes several financing options to help seniors save even more.
Memberships start at $15.58 for a Basic Plan (or $187/year). On top of helping connect people with rideshare services, GoGoGrandparent can connect you with delivery services for groceries, meals and prescriptions.
While it caters to families to with kids, HopSkipDrive.com provides transportation for anyone over the age of 6, and it's been expanding across the country. There are no upfront membership fees or monthly dues — you only pay for the rides you schedule. HopSkipDrive is a newer service and still expanding, so check out their website to see if your area is covered.
Another resource available to help senior citizens is NEMT (Non-Emergency Medical Transportation) programs, which provide free rides to medical appointments. Typically available through Medicaid and some Medicare Advantage plans, NEMT programs can be found in every state, including Alaska and Hawaii.
Seniors with visual impairment or mobility issues can also find free rides through ITNAmerica. The nonprofit transportation network helps seniors connect with free travel options through a variety of companies, ministries and charity organizations. You can find participating programs in your area at ridesinsight.org.
Other Ways Seniors Can Save on Transportation
For seniors still driving their own vehicle, AAA offers a variety of discounts and programs tailored to senior citizens, including discounts to 30,000 retailers. And if you haven't compared auto insurance rates lately, you could save hundreds of dollars.
Dial-a-ride programs can also be found across the country, usually managed by the same public transportation companies in your area. These programs, such as ACCESS LYNX in the Orlando area, work similarly to rideshare programs. They use shuttles to deliver customers to their chosen destinations, can schedule pick-up times and offer discounts for seniors.
When it comes to standard public transportation service, senior citizens can expect some form of discount. Buses, subways, trains and taxi services across the country usually offer senior discounts. Don't be afraid to ask about reduced fares.
If seniors are unable to drive, many local governments will offer free transportation as well. This will need official documents, such as a doctor's note and proof of income, but these programs are available in rural areas and urban centers across the country.

As this is all somewhat experimental, it’s worth watching to see how it all plays out in California and whether similar approaches succeed elsewhere in the country. Uber Technologies has agreed to acquire US workplace catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion in an all-cash transaction, as the ride-hailing and food delivery company seeks to expand Uber Eats into group catering and workplace meals.
Uber, in a press release on Tuesday, said that the acquisition will combine ezCater’s catering and business-to-business expertise with Uber Eats’ consumer and restaurant network and Uber for Business’ relationships with organisations, the companies said in a joint announcement.
ezCater enables businesses to order food from more than 140,000 restaurants across the US and manages workplace meals, meetings, events and recurring catering requirements. The platform generated more than $2.5 billion in gross bookings over the trailing 12 months, growing at a high-teens rate year-on-year.
The business is profitable on a non-GAAP operating income basis and is expected to be margin accretive to Uber, according to the companies. Its average order value exceeds $400, significantly positioning catering as a higher-value segment for restaurants and delivery partners.
Uber sees catering as a major revenue opportunity
“Catering is a big business, and can be a huge revenue stream for restaurants,” Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said, adding that Uber’s reach could bring ezCater’s catering experience to more customers and help restaurants capture more such orders.

Uber-ezCater deal: Why Uber is spending $2.3 billion on corporate catering
Uber will buy ezCater for $2.3 billion to expand corporate catering, grow Uber Eats and strengthen its delivery business with high-value orders.
Uber Technologies said on Tuesday that it will buy US corporate catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion in an all-cash deal. The acquisition is Uber’s latest move to grow its delivery business, which has become its fastest-growing major business segment. The deal will give Uber a bigger presence in the corporate food and catering market.
Uber is buying corporate catering platform ezCater for $2.3 billion. (Representational Photo/REUTERS)
Founded in 2007, ezCater helps companies order food from caterers for office meetings, corporate events and workplace meals. Instead of ordering individual meals, businesses can use the platform to arrange large food orders for groups of employees or event attendees. Uber said ezCater generated more than $2.5 billion in gross bookings over the past 12 months, according to Reuters.
Corporate catering can bring Uber much larger orders than normal food deliveries. Uber said the average ezCater order is worth more than $400. This means one corporate order can be worth much more than a typical individual Uber Eats order. The deal also gives Uber a new business line based on large food orders paid for by companies, rather than individual customers.

The acquisition will bring together ezCater’s catering business, Uber Eats’ restaurant network and Uber for Business’ corporate customers, Uber said. Uber can use its existing restaurant and delivery infrastructure while ezCater brings its corporate catering business, according to Reuters.
The deal also strengthens Uber’s business-focused segment, which serves corporate customers. Gross bookings in this segment grew by more than 40% in the second quarter, according to Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt. Devitt said bringing workplace buyers into Uber’s ecosystem could also help strengthen its membership business.
Uber Eats has a larger global reach, but DoorDash remains the biggest player in the US food delivery market, according to analysts cited by Reuters. Buying ezCater could help Uber close some of that gap in the US. Corporate catering gives Uber another way to attract food-delivery customers beyond regular restaurant orders.

Uber said ezCater’s average order value is above $400. The company expects the acquisition to boost margins. Larger orders can make the delivery business more valuable because Uber can generate more business from each corporate transaction.
The ezCater deal comes only months after Uber agreed in July to buy German food-delivery company Delivery Hero for $14.8 billion. That deal is aimed at creating the largest food-delivery group outside China, according to Reuters. Together, the two deals show that Uber is putting significant money into expanding its delivery operations.
Uber’s delivery business accounted for about 37% of the company’s total revenue in the second quarter. It has also been Uber’s biggest growth driver in recent times. The ezCater acquisition therefore fits into Uber’s wider strategy of making delivery a bigger part of its business.
Uber’s shares have fallen about 15% this year as investors consider how the company will compete if robotaxis changes the ride-hailing industry. The possible rise of autonomous taxis could put pressure on Uber’s traditional ride-hailing business. Expanding food delivery and corporate services gives Uber another source of growth as the future of traditional ride-hailing becomes less certain.
The deal gives Uber access to a corporate catering platform that already handles billions of dollars in bookings. It adds high-value orders, brings more companies into Uber’s ecosystem and expands Uber’s business customer base. Stop Overpaying for Uber: How to Score Senior Discounts on Rideshare Apps
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:36 AM CDT 5 min read
A little more than a decade ago, getting into a stranger's car and telling them where to take you would be viewed as ill-advised at best. But with the rise of rideshare apps like Uber, Lyft and others, nothing seems more ordinary. The system comes with a lot of benefits; it tends to be cheaper than traditional taxis, it works effectively in most places and you can get practically wherever you want to go.
Combine the rideshare phenomenon with more traditional modes of transportation, and the world has gotten more mobile than ever before with plenty of options to travel. Alas, almost all those options still cost money. Luckily for seniors, there are also plenty of opportunities to save money while getting around.

How to Score Senior Discounts on Ridesharing Apps
The bigger rideshare companies all have their own apps, and if you know what to look for, there are loads of ways to save.
When using any of these apps, keep an eye out for promo codes that can help you save even more. In recent promotions, Lyft and Uber both advertise promo codes which give up to 50% discounts to new riders, regardless of your age.
Lyft doesn't offer a generalized senior discount for their basic service, but through their Lyft Silver program, seniors can use a simplified interface, find better vehicle matches (easier entry and exit) and get support to book their ride through Lyft.
Lyft's subscription service Lyft Pink does offer discounts with plans starting at $9.99 (or $99/year). For those who need to travel on a regular basis or have a busy schedule, Pink can help you save a bundle.
Additionally, many cities partner with Lyft to offer discounted rides to those 60 and older. In Charleston, South Carolina, CARTA offers seniors Lyft or Uber trips for as little as $5 each way within a fixed-route area.
Similar to Lyft, Uber doesn't offer a specific senior discount, but it does partner with municipalities to offer discounted rides for those 60 and older.
Also similar to Lyft, if you're a frequent rider, you can save money with a membership. An Uber One membership costs $9.99 (or $96/year) and lets you earn 5% back on rides and includes a $0 delivery fee for food and grocery orders.
GoGoGrandparent.com connects you to rideshare services and arranges deliveries of groceries and medications. Despite the name, anyone over 18 can order a ride and you can use it from any phone that generates tones by the press of a button — meaning, you don't need a smartphone. It features a simple menu and a live service that can help customers find the best and cheapest options. It also includes several financing options to help seniors save even more.
Memberships start at $15.58 for a Basic Plan (or $187/year). On top of helping connect people with rideshare services, GoGoGrandparent can connect you with delivery services for groceries, meals and prescriptions.
While it caters to families to with kids, HopSkipDrive.com provides transportation for anyone over the age of 6, and it's been expanding across the country. There are no upfront membership fees or monthly dues — you only pay for the rides you schedule. HopSkipDrive is a newer service and still expanding, so check out their website to see if your area is covered.
Another resource available to help senior citizens is NEMT (Non-Emergency Medical Transportation) programs, which provide free rides to medical appointments. Typically available through Medicaid and some Medicare Advantage plans, NEMT programs can be found in every state, including Alaska and Hawaii.
Seniors with visual impairment or mobility issues can also find free rides through ITNAmerica. The nonprofit transportation network helps seniors connect with free travel options through a variety of companies, ministries and charity organizations. You can find participating programs in your area at ridesinsight.org.
Other Ways Seniors Can Save on Transportation
For seniors still driving their own vehicle, AAA offers a variety of discounts and programs tailored to senior citizens, including discounts to 30,000 retailers. And if you haven't compared auto insurance rates lately, you could save hundreds of dollars.
Dial-a-ride programs can also be found across the country, usually managed by the same public transportation companies in your area. These programs, such as ACCESS LYNX in the Orlando area, work similarly to rideshare programs. They use shuttles to deliver customers to their chosen destinations, can schedule pick-up times and offer discounts for seniors.
When it comes to standard public transportation service, senior citizens can expect some form of discount. Buses, subways, trains and taxi services across the country usually offer senior discounts. Don't be afraid to ask about reduced fares.
If seniors are unable to drive, many local governments will offer free transportation as well. This will need official documents, such as a doctor's note and proof of income, but these programs are available in rural areas and urban centers across the country.
